test_title: PYST 42 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Complete the sentence with the most appropriate preposition:

International organisations worked together to launch initiatives aimed ___ increasing female literacy rates.
solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4 (At)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: On***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “On increasing” is not idiomatic in this context; it would sound awkward and ungrammatical.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: For***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “Aimed for increasing” is not standard usage. “For” works with nouns (“aimed for success”), but not with gerunds like “increasing.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: To***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. “Aimed to increasing” is grammatically wrong. “To” would require the base verb (“aimed to increase”), not the gerund “increasing.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: At***
 
 
• This is **correct**. The standard collocation is “aimed at + gerund/noun.” Hence, “aimed at increasing female literacy rates” is the proper construction.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4 (At)**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The verb phrase **“aimed at”** is a fixed collocation in English, used when describing goals directed toward an action or outcome.
 
• Examples: “The policy is aimed at reducing poverty.” / “The campaign is aimed at raising awareness.”
 
• This construction highlights the **purpose or target** of the initiative.
